methods.title: Severe weather score.
methods.text: Expected yearly storm damage to an average home from tornadoes (40%), hail (40%) and strong wind (20%), from the FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025 release), ranked across Oklahoma ZIP codes. 0 is the lowest in the state and 100 the highest. Low 0-39, Moderate 40-69, High 70-89, Extreme 90-100. All of Oklahoma is above the national average for hail and tornadoes, so these tiers compare places within the state.

methods.title: Wildfire score.
methods.text: Average of two public measures for the homes in each area: FEMA National Risk Index wildfire damage per home (December 2025) and the USDA Forest Service Wildfire Risk to Communities risk to homes (2nd edition, 2024 release). Each home is placed against all U.S. homes, then areas are ranked within Oklahoma using the same tier ranges. These public measures approximate, but do not replicate, carrier scores such as Verisk FireLine.

methods.title: Prime targets.
methods.text: Low or Moderate on both risk layers, at least 70% of homes owner-occupied, median household income at or above the Oklahoma median ($65,039), and at least 1,000 owner-occupied homes. Review list: High or Extreme on either risk layer.

methods.title: Homes and income.
methods.text: U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates. ZIP codes are Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas; areas are matched to risk data using 2020 Census housing counts. Gray areas inside the state have no ZIP code (parks, military land, lakes).

methods.title: Recent storms.
methods.text: NOAA Storm Events Database and Storm Prediction Center tornado tracks, 2015-2025 compared with 1990-2014.
